text:
m1 - PARTITION DELIVERED, and I found a MECHANICAL CRITERION that is better than case-by-case reachability, because it is checkable by reading one line.

THE CRITERION: GUARD POLARITY DECIDES WHETHER NaN FAILS OPEN OR CLOSED.

  `if x <= 0.0 then SAFE else COMPUTE`   NaN -> comparison false -> ELSE -> COMPUTE runs on NaN.  FAILS OPEN.
  `if x >  0.0 then COMPUTE else SAFE`   NaN -> comparison false -> ELSE -> SAFE.                 FAILS CLOSED.

Both guards are "the same check". Only the polarity differs, and it inverts the outcome. Verified against the known defect: importanceWeightedCoverage is `if wsum <= 0 then Missing else Observed(...)` - fails open, publishes Observed(NaN). Exactly as the rule records it.

This is why the population is not the finding. THE POLARITY IS.

FAILS OPEN - NaN reaches the arithmetic:
  features/window.scala:122   if tw <= 0.0 then undefined else Estimate.observed(... / tw)
  align/signature.scala:93    MassRatio.support        (MINE)
  align/signature.scala:111   MassRatio.unsafe         (MINE)
  align/population.scala:266  if totalFlow <= 0.0 then Missing
  align/population.scala:177  if m <= 0.0 then 0.0 else 1.0 - exp(-m)
  align/matrix.scala:175,217  sourceMass / z
  align/density.scala:154     if z <= 0.0 then uniform else raw.map(_ / z)
  align/hsmm.scala:794        if z <= 0.0 then None else Some(pairs.sum / z)
  amr Smatch.scala:28         if p + r == 0.0 then 0.0 else 2pr/(p+r)
  interview/assess.scala:112  if total <= 0.0 then ...

FAILS CLOSED - safe by construction, no work needed:
  features/window.scala:129, 158   if tw > 0.0 then observed(...) else <fallback>
  align/source.scala:223           if w > 0.0 then enqueue
  align/signature.scala:302        if m > 0.0 then ...

THREE I WOULD LOOK AT BEFORE THE REST:

1. sinkhorn.scala:44 IS A VALIDATOR THAT FAILS OPEN, which is the worst shape here:
     else if config.epsilon <= 0.0 || rhoRows < 0.0 || rhoCols < 0.0 then Left(InvalidConfig)
   A NaN epsilon passes ALL THREE comparisons, the config is ACCEPTED, and every entry of the cost
   matrix becomes -c / NaN = NaN. This is precisely the rule's "a checked constructor with an
   internal unsafe path is making a false claim about itself" - except it is a validator, so the
   false claim is its entire purpose.

2. features/window.scala:122 IS A SECOND LIVE INSTANCE OF THE EXACT DEFECT the rule was written
   about, in a different module. `if tw <= 0.0 then undefined else Estimate.observed(sum / tw)` -
   same shape as wsum, same Estimate.observed(NaN) outcome. Its two SIBLINGS at :129 and :158 use
   the safe polarity, so the file contains both forms fifteen lines apart, which is the same
   "no convention" signature as the empty-guard sweep.

3. signature.scala:93 and :111 ARE MINE. MassRatio.unsafe takes `if conditioning <= 0.0 then None
   else Some(numerator / conditioning)` - a NaN conditioning yields Some(NaN), a value asserting a
   measurement was made. I wrote the carrier whose entire purpose is to refuse unsupported numbers,
   and gave it a guard that admits the least supported number there is.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE, and the bead is right to insist on it: THIS IS NOT REACHABILITY. Polarity says
what happens IF NaN arrives. It does not say NaN can arrive. Most of these take sums of masses that
are validated non-NaN upstream, so many will be unreachable in practice - the same way three of the
sixteen empty-guard sites turned out to be correct-as-written. The next step is reachability per
site, and it is a different and slower job.

But the polarity partition is worth having on its own, because it is MECHANICAL: `grep` for `<= 0.0
then` versus `> 0.0 then` sorts the population without judgement, and the fail-closed half needs no
further thought at all.
